page.layout: One page of text, single column. Running head at top, with page number at left. No margin notes. Heading "ALTERA PARS VERSVS", then a title line with the Greek word, then verse paragraph and closing paragraph.

main_text.p: laudanda vituperantium, præiudicium ingratum esse debet. Non tam enim quis de nobis pronūciet, quàm quomodo, & quàm vere, utiliter & appositè pronunciet, nobis est considerandum.

II. Iniusta autè præiudicia, calumnias, vellicationes, æquis feramus animis: ac memores simus dicti Prophetæ de viro beato: Ab auditu malo non trepidabit: firmum est cor eius cōfidens in Iehouah. Psal.112.7.
Hæc de alienis iudicijs, de nobisipsis & vita nostra, paucis licuit ἐπιαγχαφάν[?]. Vos pro vestra diligentia & pietate, addetis quæ huc facere videbuntur.
main_text.head: ALTERA PARS VERSVS
6. de πλεονεξίᾳ[?] Nebucadnezaris, & opibus male partis.

p.i: Væ multiplicanti non sua: & quousque id faciet, & aggravabit super se lutum de-sum? id est, opes terrenas, οἵτινες βυθίζωσι[?] τὰς ἀνθρώπως εἰς ὄλεθρον καὶ[?] ἀπώλειαν. 1. Timoth.6.9.

main_text.p: Hac exclamatione Dominus ostedit, Nebucadnezaris insatiabilem esse φιλαρ-χίαν

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the Roman numeral before "Iniusta" (read as II); the Greek word after "ἐπι" in the "Hæc de alienis" paragraph; the Greek word for "avarice/ambition" in the heading (read as πλεονεξίᾳ); the Greek verb "βυθίζωσι" and the Greek article/word "καὶ" in the 1 Timothy quotation; the Greek word "ἀνθρώπως" is printed as shown and may be a printing error for "ἀνθρώπους". The line break "de-/sum" is read as densum, with the hyphen kept as printed. "Væ" is kept with æ as printed. The final Greek word is split across the line end as "φιλαρ-/χίαν". No margin notes, catchword or signature are visible. Page number 234 is at the head left.
